milestone.title: mp autopilot hard gate — refuse to start without herdr ≥ 0.7.x

intent.outcome: `mp autopilot start` refuses to run if `herdr` is not on PATH or if its version is below 0.7.x; the error message includes an install hint (command to install herdr) and a link to the upgrade docs. The gate is mandatory; `--force` does not bypass it (herdr is a hard architectural requirement, not a convenience).

problem.description: M197 built the herdr version-gate machinery (in `crates/mp/src/watch/herdr_version.rs`) but only as a precondition for `mp watch` — silently falling back to surface the diagnostic at spawn time. The new autopilot design treats herdr as a hard architectural requirement (one pane-set, three roles, workspace naming all depend on it). A missing or incompatible herdr must be a hard refusal, not a diagnostic surface, because the user's mental model is 'this is an automation that drives the milestone through a real workspace,' not 'this is a CLI that shells out to herdr.'

in_scope: `mp autopilot start` invokes the M197 `detect_herdr_cli` precondition early in the command pipeline. If `which herdr` returns nothing, error with: 'mp autopilot requires herdr installed; install via <brew|build from source>: <command>'. Exit code 78 (EX_CONFIG).
If herdr is found but its shape / version flag doesn't match 0.7.x, error with: 'mp autopilot requires herdr >= 0.7.x; detected <version>; upgrade via <command>'. Same exit code.
The gate is wired into the same precondition function used by `mp watch` today; refactor so both call sites share the code path.

Surface the gate in `mp doctor` (project health) — already partially shipped in M197, expand to surface the autopilot-specific error string when invoked from a plan that has autopilot/ in its master-plan/.
out_of_scope: Removing the diagnostic but non-blocking path from `mp doctor` — that's a product call; the gate stays as a non-blocking doctor surface for visibility even when `mp autopilot start` is not invoked.

Replacing the M178 fallback "herdr spawn failed with diagnostics" — that's still the right behavior when herdr is present but a specific spawn fails; this milestone elevates presence+version to a hard gate.
Harness-specific policies for which versions of opencode/cursor/pi are required — out of scope; the gate is herdr-only.

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp autopilot start` with herdr absent exits 78 before creating a session directory, writing plan state, or invoking any spawn operation; the diagnostic contains an install hint.

Semantic-version checking accepts every compatible herdr version >=0.7.0 whose required command shape is present, rejects lower versions or incompatible shapes with exit 78, and reports detected version plus upgrade hint.
The precondition function is called by both `mp autopilot start` and `mp watch` (legacy alias) — no divergence in gate behavior between the two.
`mp doctor` reports autopilot herdr availability, detected version/shape, compatibility result, and install/upgrade guidance without making the overall doctor command mutating.

design_decisions.choice: Exit 78 (EX_CONFIG from sysexits.h) — matches the 'configuration error, not a runtime error' semantics.
design_decisions.rationale: Allows shell scripts to distinguish 'herdr missing/old' (configuration) from 'milestone failed' (runtime) by exit code alone.

design_decisions.choice: `--force` does NOT bypass the herdr gate. herdr is required by design; `--force` keeps its existing role (bypass double-spawn guard, M178).
design_decisions.rationale: Bypassing the gate leaves the user with a session that has no workspace — every other step depends on herdr being usable.
